- SOARecord: already test.

- NoRRset: use a Record with name/type not present.

- NS single: zone already has only one NS -> test exists.

- Multi A: create zone with two A records same name; test removal of one leaves other.

- Single A no NS: removal of sole A record should remove RRset but not NS.

- NS multiple: zone with multiple NS records; removal of one should keep NS set.

- NS single with signature: zone with NS record + RRSIG for NS; removal should keep RRset.

- Record not in RRset: zone has A RRset with a1; attempt to remove a mock A record with same name/type but not same instance; deleteRR called but no effect; after removal, original record still present. We can test that.

- Last RRset removes name: zone with a single TXT record for orphan.example.com. After removal, findExactMatch for that name/type returns null and zone.findExactMatch for any other type maybe null; also zone.iterator should not contain that name. Simpler: check that zone.findExactMatch returns null and that zone.getNS() still present.

- NonNS single with other RRsets present: zone with NS and A; remove sole A record; ensure NS still present.

Simplify: Use Mockito to mock RRset and inject into zone's internal map via reflection. We'll attempt to find field "rrsets" maybe a map. Let's inspect typical implementation of Zone in dnsjava library. I recall Zone uses ConcurrentSkipListMap<Name, Map<Integer, RRset>> maybe. In dnsjava, there is a field "rrsets" of type ConcurrentSkipListMap<Name, Map<Integer, RRset>>. So we can reflectively access that and put our mock RRset.

We'll write utility method to inject mock RRset.

Thus we cannot verify internal call directly; we will rely on state.
